answer: Each identity files one row in the open tide table: a violet stamp from its key plus a kernel receipt of its finished job. Auditors replay the table; a copied row or shared kernel receipt burns its 60-credit bond. Filing starts at 40, rising 4 per row, so 1,000 fakes cost 2,038,000 plus 60,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. Rented rows fail: the kernel receipt must match the filer's key. Honest agents file one true row, pay 40 once, keep the bond.
